study_identification_part.si4_title: Individualized cortical thickness asymmetry in Autism Spectrum Disorders and Schizophrenia

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The abstract clearly states the study’s objective: to investigate the degree of individual-level abnormal cortical thickness asymmetry in ASD and SZ using normative modeling, and to evaluate regional and individual deviance patterns and their diagnostic relevance.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Cortical thickness asymmetry has been proposed as a latent biomarker for Autism Spectrum Disorders (ASD) and schizophrenia (SZ)... To investigate this, we applied normative modeling."; "Regional deviance was assessed... We also evaluated individual deviance... A data-driven multivariate approach was employed to determine whether joint regional deviance was associated with diagnosis."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: The study builds a new normative model. It describes image quality standards and exclusion criteria (CAT12 IQR > 2.8; Euler number threshold), reports final sample sizes, and references prior QC for specific datasets. However, explicit eligibility/inclusion criteria for healthy controls and complete citations to original dataset publications are not fully detailed in the main text.
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "We examined data for 5430 healthy individuals... taken from 20 different scan sites."; "Using the... Computational Anatomy Toolbox to generate a weighted overall image quality rating (IQR)... we excluded 682 images with an IQR >2.8."; "All remaining images were processed... FreeSurfer (v7.1)... images were removed if the ... Euler number was larger than 10... This was the case for five images."; "The scanner details, sample size, demographic and clinical characteristics of each scan site... are presented in Supplemental Table 1."; "The training set consisted of 4904 healthy individuals..."

nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.reason: Age, sex, Euler number (image quality), and scanner were included as covariates in the normative model; a within-site split was used and site-effects were further examined via site-classification analyses.
nm2_handling_of_covariates_reference_coh.supporting_text: "Including age, sex, Euler number, and scanner as covariates..."; "Both the training and test sets comprised individuals from the same scanners, constituting a 'within-site-split'."

nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.reason: The study specifies multi-site sources and lists dataset/site names in the supplement (e.g., ABIDE-I NYU, ABIDE-II GU, COBRE, UTRECHT, AOMIC, CAMCAN, IXI, OASIS, ROCKLAND).
nm3_data_sources_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "We examined data... from 20 different scan sites."; Supplemental Table entries include: "ABIDE-I NYU", "ABIDE-II OHSU", "COBRE", "UTRECHT", "AOMIC-ID1000", "CAMCAN", "IXI", "OASIS", "ROCKLAND".

nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.reason: Secondary data were used from existing datasets across 20 sites; per guide, image acquisition protocol is not applicable when using secondary data.
nm4_image_acquisition_protocol.supporting_text: "We examined data... from 20 different scan sites."

nm5_data_preprocessing.reason: Preprocessing is described: central FreeSurfer processing (v7.1) with default settings; Euler number extraction for QC; additional asymmetry processing using FreeSurfer qcache and xhemi for an alternative pipeline; quality control thresholds specified.
nm5_data_preprocessing.supporting_text: "All remaining images were processed centrally using the FreeSurfer analysis suite (v7.1) with default settings... The Freesurfer Euler number was extracted... images were removed if... Euler number was larger than 10..."; "We generated unsmoothed vertex-wise standard space cortical thickness maps... using Freesurfer's 'qcache'... inserted into Freesurfer's 'xhemi'..."

nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.reason: They employed 10-fold cross-validation within the training cohort to evaluate generalization and computed z-scores and RMSE in cross-validation.
nm6_internal_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "We employed a ten-fold cross-validation approach on the training cohort... This process was repeated ten times... Z-scores were calculated and we assessed model fit by calculating the root-mean squared error..."

nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.reason: The model was not evaluated on an independent external healthy dataset separate from development; the held-out cohort was a within-site split from the same scanners.
nm7_external_data_validation_reference_c.supporting_text: "Both the training and test sets comprised individuals from the same scanners, constituting a 'within-site-split'."

nm8_normative_modeling_approach.reason: The statistical approach is specified as Bayesian Linear Regression with key covariates and uncertainty decomposition described. However, software/library used for the normative modeling implementation is not explicitly stated.
nm8_normative_modeling_approach.supporting_text: "Subsequently, we used Bayesian Linear Regression (Fraza et al., 2021)..."; "The difference... is normalized to account for... aleatoric uncertainty... and... epistemic uncertainty..."

nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.reason: Model fit is quantitatively assessed using RMSE between predicted and true AI values; additional performance visualization provided in supplemental figures.
nm9_model_performance_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "We assessed model fit by calculating the root-mean squared error between predicted and true AI values... see Supplemental Figures 3, 5 and 10."

nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.reason: They report the partitioning scheme (90/10 per dataset) and state that the distributions of age, sex, and scanner were maintained between training and test sets. However, detailed demographic characteristics per partition are not reported.
nm10_characteristics_reference_cohort_ea.supporting_text: "For each of the datasets... 90%... into the training set and 10% into the test set... We maintained the distribution of age, sex, and scanner variables between the training and test sets."

nm11_reproducibility.reason: Some software details are provided (FreeSurfer v7.1; R packages such as caret and coin are mentioned). However, explicit versions for all software and libraries used for normative modeling and statements on code/model/data availability are not provided.
nm11_reproducibility.supporting_text: "Processed centrally using the FreeSurfer analysis suite (v7.1)..."; "...using the createDataPartition function from the caret R package... using the coin R package..."

cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.reason: Secondary clinical data were aggregated from multiple datasets. The study reports image quality standards and exclusions and provides final clinical sample sizes, but does not detail diagnostic eligibility criteria (e.g., DSM/ICD) for cases within the main text.
cr1_selection_criteria_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "The clinical sample comprised 135 individuals with ASD... and 287 individuals with SZ..."; "We... applied the Computational Anatomy Toolbox... IQR... excluded 682 images..."; "images were removed if... Euler number was larger than 10..."; "scanner details, sample size, demographic and clinical characteristics... presented in Supplemental Table 1."

cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.reason: Analyses of deviation scores do not include clinical covariates such as medication status or illness duration. Robustness checks examine handedness and IQ, but these are not modeled as covariates in the primary analyses of deviations.
cr2_handling_of_clinical_covariates.supporting_text: "To assess the robustness of our results we... assessed the effect of handedness and IQ on the average z-scores..."

cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.reason: Clinical cases were drawn from named multi-site datasets; the supplement lists specific datasets contributing ASD and SZ cases (e.g., ABIDE sites, COBRE, UTRECHT).
cr3_data_sources_clinical_cohort.supporting_text: "We examined data... from 20 different scan sites."; Supplemental dataset list includes ABIDE-I/II sites, COBRE, UTRECHT, etc.

cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.reason: Sample sizes and sex distribution are reported overall, and age distributions per site are shown in a supplemental figure. However, detailed clinical characteristics (e.g., medication, symptom scales, illness duration) are not reported.
cr4_clinical_characteristics_clinical_co.supporting_text: "The clinical sample comprised 135 individuals with ASD (83% male) and 287 individuals with SZ (81% male). The age distributions per scan site are given in Supplemental Figure 1."

cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.reason: The paper does not describe clinical assessment instruments or diagnostic procedures (e.g., ADOS, PANSS, DSM/ICD criteria) used in the contributing datasets.
cr5_clinical_assessment_measures.supporting_text: "...multi-center studies... including datasets lacking deep phenotyping. Hence, information about handedness, IQ and symptomatology was incomplete."

cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.reason: The direction and meaning of AI and deviation scores are defined (positive AI = leftward), quantitative thresholds (|z| ≥ 1.96) are specified for infra-/supra-normal deviations, and clinical implications are discussed, noting limited diagnostic differentiation and challenging biomarker utility.
cr6_interpretation_of_deviation_scores.supporting_text: "A positive AI value reflects leftward asymmetry (LH > RH)."; "As per prior publications we considered AI z-scores as infra- or supra-normal when they equalled or exceeded -1.96 or 1.96, respectively."; "Multivariate analysis showed no association between inter-regional heterogeneity of AI and diagnosis... This study challenges the utility of cortical thickness asymmetry as a biomarker for ASD."
